description: The plot illustrates the relationship between temperature and Pass@8 accuracy, comparing the performance of three methods: On-policy RL, LUFFY, and SFT. The x-axis represents temperature, with a linear scale ranging from 0.1 to 1.0, and tick labels at intervals of 0.1. The y-axis represents accuracy, with a linear scale ranging from 62.5 to 80.0, and tick labels at intervals of 2.5. The On-policy RL line, colored yellow with triangle markers and a solid line style, starts at approximately 63.0 at a temperature of 0.1, fluctuates between 67.5 and 72.5 up to a temperature of 0.8, and ends at 73.0 at a temperature of 1.0. The LUFFY line, colored red with star markers and a solid line style, begins at 76.0 at a temperature of 0.1, remains relatively stable with minor fluctuations between 75.0 and 81.0, and ends at 80.0 at a temperature of 1.0. The SFT line, colored teal with inverted triangle markers and a solid line style, starts at 73.0 at a temperature of 0.1, decreases to 68.0 at a temperature of 0.5, then increases to 74.0 at a temperature of 1.0, showing variability across the temperature range.
caption_used: The line plot illustrates Pass@8 accuracy across varying generation temperatures, measured on the merged sets of AIME 2024 and AMC. The 'On-policy RL' line (yellow, triangle markers) shows a steady increase from approximately 63.0 at 0.1 to 75.0 at 0.8, followed by a slight decline to 73.0 at 1.0. The 'LUFFY' line (red, star markers) demonstrates consistent superiority, starting at 76.0 at 0.1 and peaking at 81.0 at 0.8, before stabilizing at 80.0 at 1.0. The 'SFT' line (teal, inverted triangle markers) begins at 73.0 at 0.1, dips sharply to 68.0 at 0.5, and recovers to 74.0 at 1.0, showing the most variability among the three methods. Overall, LUFFY consistently outperforms the other methods across all temperature settings, with On-policy RL showing the most significant improvement over time.
